# SMESH

> A Rust protocol for coordinating agents through signals that diffuse, decay and get reinforced. Consensus emerges from reinforcement rather than voting, with no central coordinator.

This site replays one recorded, read-only quant research run. Every count on it comes from data/replay.json, exported from the run's journal with `smesh quant export-site`.

## What it is

- Signals: messages with an intensity that decays over time; reinforcement restores them.
- Field: the shared space signals live on. A claim nothing reinforces fades away.
- Settlement: agents claim tasks with their own affinity and back off from stronger claims.
- A2A v1.0: the mesh serves as one A2A agent and can recruit other A2A agents as members.
- Jev (TypeSafe AI): agents described in plain language judge for themselves whether they suit a task.

## The study on this page

- Venues: Kalshi (public market data, unsigned), Massive (licensed key), Kraken (public trades). Read-only by construction: only GET to allowlisted market-data paths.
- Crypto track: Kalshi hourly BTC/ETH above/below odds 30 minutes before close vs a realized-volatility model, walk-forward with fee-aware paper trading.
- Macro track: Kalshi CPI, payrolls and Fed ladders an hour before release vs the actual print, last print and climatology; SPY/TLT reaction to the surprise.
- Hypotheses are signals on a SMESH field. Consensus means a final strength of 0.30 or more.
- Limits: one recorded period; several claims share windows; macro windows hold one release each. Not trading advice.
